If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract downward bias.

If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3 days, apply a 2–3% downward correction to forecast starting at day 7, especially if true outcome shows sharp decline.

If sentiment is mixed (±0.33–0.67) and forecast shows rising trend, reduce forecast by 1–2% for late horizon (16–30 days) to dampen overconfidence in sustained growth.

If sentiment is positive but true outcome shows early divergence (e.g., +2% above forecast within first 3 days), apply a 1–1.5% downward adjustment to forecast from day 4 onward to align with sentiment-driven volatility.

If sentiment is negative and forecast shows early overcorrection (e.g., -2% below true within first 3 days), apply a 1–1.5% upward adjustment to forecast from day 4 onward to avoid premature pessimism.
